A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QUESTA research. All pages, including appendices, are readable, and the text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v3 reports original RL experiments, mathematical reasoning benchmark results, curriculum and hint ablations, and cross-domain evaluations in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results in Section 5 and Appendix D and additionally reports success-count distributions across hint levels in Appendix B.6.

M1.justification: Partial-solution augmentation, difficulty filtering, the 50%-to-25% curriculum, and the GRPO/DAPO-based training objective remain unchanged. Appendix B.6 explains the existing hint choices without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use OpenR1 and OpenMathReasoning training data and retain the same mathematics, knowledge, logic, and coding benchmarks. The added hint-percentage analysis stays within the existing OpenR1 mathematical reasoning coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark tables and corresponding controlled experiments and ablations. Newly cited WizardMath and R3 are discussed as related work, without being added to the reported experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: v4 adds a pre-training evaluation across 0%, 10%, 25%, and 50% hints on the first-filtered OpenR1 subset, recording correct-answer counts from eight completions per problem. Existing training budgets, filtering rules, benchmark metrics, and evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.6 adds a hint-level sensitivity analysis examining how the supplied solution fraction changes initial problem solvability. The curriculum, no-hint, alternative-backbone, alternative-dataset, and training-dynamics analyses already present in v3 are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 32-sample benchmark averaging, eight-completion difficulty measurements, and the same unbiased pass@k estimator. The new table uses the existing eight-completion practice; neither version reports independent training-seed uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports success-count distributions across hint levels, including 17,741 problems solved 8/8 times with Partial-50, 7,159 with Partial-25, and 6,506 with Partial-10. Existing benchmark values, unsolved-problem indices, ablation scores, and plotted results remain unchanged after matching v3 Tables 5–7 to v4 Tables 6–8.

T1.justification: Section 4 retains the same definitions, assumptions, and learnability theorems. The appendix proofs and tabular-policy analysis move from Appendix B to Appendix C with corresponding renumbering but no substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, three stated contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about reasoning capacity, sample efficiency, and state-of-the-art 1.5B performance. The headline AIME24, AIME25, and HMMT25 results are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix B.6 newly interprets 50% hints as substantially reducing difficulty and 25% hints as close to the no-hint condition, using this to motivate the curriculum and infer limited additional training benefit. The introduction also adds a contrast between difficulty diversity in SFT and easy-prompt effects in RLVR.

D1.justification: Beyond the public repository disclosure already in v3, v4 Section 8 states that supplementary artifacts and an anonymous repository include a step-by-step reproduction README. Section 7 adds dataset-license information. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and prompt templates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds WizardMath (Luo et al., 2025a) to contextualize difficulty diversity and R3 (Xi et al., 2024) as prior work using preceding solution steps for RL. These are limited additions to related-work coverage; the broader positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main narrative are retained. v4 adds a short introductory comparison, a hint-choice subsection, ethics/reproducibility/funding sections, and an LLM-use appendix, with corresponding cross-reference updates and small curriculum-wording clarifications.

P2.justification: v4 adds the hint-distribution table, introduces conference headers, and reflows existing tables, figures, and prompt boxes across pages. The existing figures retain their graphical content, while the later appendix tables are renumbered rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The added hint-level measurements provide useful evidence about the existing curriculum, while the additional related-work coverage and explicit reproduction instructions modestly improve completeness. These gains are limited because the main results and theory remain unchanged. Appendix B.6 also overinterprets pre-training success distributions as evidence about subsequent training benefit, weakening its explanatory contribution without outweighing the useful additions.
